Custom icons for apps that aren't pinned now show on the taskbar.

**Download `iconger.exe` below**, or open Iconger: it will offer the update itself.

## Fixed (experimental feature)
- In v0.8.0 the new icon of an app that isn't pinned only showed in Alt+Tab and the app's title bar, not on its taskbar button. The taskbar takes a button's icon from the app's identity rather than from its window, so Iconger now also gives the app's windows an identity of their own that carries your icon (the same thing Chrome does to show a different icon for each profile).
- Because of that, the app's taskbar button may move to a new spot when the icon is applied, and its jump list (the recent files you see on right-click) isn't shown while the custom icon is on. Restoring the icon puts both back.
- Tip: pin the button from the taskbar and the pin keeps your icon. It then behaves like any other pin, no background needed.

Your backups and settings carry over.
